To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p04
Cc: none
Subject: none

Priya, I’m very sorry you’re dealing with this. I’m a chartered structural engineer, but I haven’t been asked to inspect the building and this isn’t a commission. I have no professional indemnity cover for free advice. I’m speaking only as a neighbour who looked from the pavement opposite at about 7 this morning.

From there, I could see about 1.2 metres of chimney still standing on no. 41, leaning towards no. 43, with mortar visibly washed out at the base. There’s a hole of roughly 2–3 square metres in no. 43’s front roof, a stepped crack above the bay about 5–10mm wide, and the bay head looks to have dropped. I couldn’t see inside or assess the party wall. These observations aren’t enough to say the buildings are safe.

Please don’t let Mick or anyone else go into no. 43 to put props up or inspect the loft. Propping beneath a roof that’s been holed, with a loose chimney stack above, could put someone in the worst place if anything shifts. Debris may also have loaded the floors, and nobody can safely assume what is carrying what now. This needs assessment by the council’s dangerous structures officer or an appropriately appointed professional—not a DIY intervention.

The council’s out-of-hours dangerous structures service is reached via the main council number. They know about this, but the pavement still wasn’t closed when I looked. There are loose slates above it, so I’d keep well away and walk on the other side of the road, especially for the school run, until the council has attended and made it safe.

I can’t decide for Mrs Doherty whether to leave, and I can’t say from outside that no. 45 is safe. Its front looked undamaged, but that isn’t a proper assessment. If she’s willing, I wouldn’t sleep in the front room tonight; staying with family until no. 45 has been checked would be the cautious choice. Please contact the council urgently about her as well.
